scenes.spoken_text: Support design starts with load paths, the supporting substrate and access for service. Distinguish bearing support from restraint without turning a sketch into a universal fixing prescription.
scenes.caption: Support design starts with load paths, the supporting substrate and access for service. Distinguish bearing support from restraint without turning a sketch into a universal fixing prescription.

scenes.display_title: Trace load paths and support type
scenes.spoken_text: A floor-standing unit transfers weight through its parts and base or legs to the floor. A wall-hung unit transfers it through carcass connections and suspension to the wall. These paths define the review scope, not adequacy. Distinguish vertical weight from a user pull at a handle and identify bearing and restraint points for each use case.
scenes.caption: Floor-bearing and wall-hung load paths differ.

scenes.display_title: Identify the substrate and fixing system
scenes.spoken_text: Paint or tile does not identify the load-bearing substrate. Document its construction, condition and concealed services using site information. The detail must show carcass, support member, carcass-to-support connection and support-to-substrate connection. Fixing type, number, size and location require system-specific technical review; this lesson provides planning, not drilling instructions.
scenes.caption: Review both carcass-to-support and support-to-substrate connections.

scenes.spoken_text: A cover may hide adjustment or fixing points; define access without destroying finishes. Draw cover removal and service sequence, identifying any temporary support needed in a competent specialist’s plan. Do not treat a load-carrying connection as a freely removable cover. Retain system references, fixing locations and inspection records with approved maintenance instructions.
scenes.caption: Service access must preserve the required support plan.

scenes.spoken_text: Option A shows a screw into a finish without identifying its substrate. B shows carcass, support, substrate and both connections, flagging load and substrate information for review. B is a more complete review package because it exposes the load path and unknowns; it is not installation approval. Decision: develop B as a review package; do not issue it for installation before technical verification.
scenes.caption: Decision: develop B as a review package; do not issue it for installation before technical verification.
